relevance_note: Reports individual GFAP carriers with Alexander disease in three families, e.g. 'the two other affected children (II.c, II.f) also tested positive for the p.Ser247Pro mutation'.
method_note: Worked from the full text by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked that every span occurs verbatim. Scope: the three families (A, B, C), including tested-negative relatives (II.b, I.b, V.C, I.1, I.2), untested Family B members the paper names with individual facts (III.A and III.E, brothers of III.F 'considered potentially affected'; IV.D and IV.F, daughters of III.F called 'adult-onset patients' in the Figure 1 legend), and previously published people in the Discussion with individual-level facts (Namekawa^18 brothers; the Shiihara^20 p.Leu331Pro boy, his sister and mother; two people from the Stumpf^21 p.Asp78Glu family). Siblings of Family A beyond II.b-II.f, the other siblings of Family C II.1, and the parents of the Namekawa brothers (not tested, not affected) get no rows. The Stumpf juvenile-onset individual ('ref 21 patient') has no variant row: the paper never states that this person carries p.Asp78Glu, only that it is 'the p.Asp78Glu family'. II.c and II.d are mapped by the Figure 1 legend to Duckett et al.^3, III.F to Seil et al.^2, IV.B/IV.D/IV.F to Schwankhaus et al.^8; I copied those into source_reference_in_review to support cross-paper merging although the paper adds new first-hand data for II.c, II.d and IV.B. cDNA changes are printed without 'c.' (739T→C, 1250A→C, 1277A→T) and were recorded as printed; the cDNA is printed only for the first-sequenced person of each family (II.d, VI.A, II.1), so other carriers have the protein string only. Ages at 'presented' were recorded as onset for II.d, III.F and VI.A (presentation for symptoms); for II.c the onset text is the presentation age with a 1-year history (no ISO given, since it would need arithmetic); for II.f onset is 'during her early 20’s'. Head circumferences (II.d 59.5 cm, II.f 58 cm, both 98%) were not called macrocephaly by the paper, so macrocephaly is not reported for them. 'Incoordination' (II.c) and 'progressive deterioration in balance' (II.f) were not mapped to the ataxia checklist item; 'generalized weakness' (V.B) was not mapped to limb weakness; II.f's 'episode of atonia, with inability to move her arms and legs' and III.F's arm paralysis were mapped to limb weakness. 'no megalencephaly' (Shiihara sister and mother) does not exclude the composite item 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly' (narrow/broad rule). Broad statements ('no known neurological or cognitive deficits', 'no neurological symptoms', 'asymptomatic') were recorded as written and excluded nothing more specific, except cognitive decline for II.b and II.e (cognitive deficits are named). VI.A's periventricular rim is from CT, not MRI. III.1's cause of death is not stated (only the circumstances: found unresponsive with blood alcohol 0.22%). Contradictions in the paper: (1) father I.a 'died at the age of 66' (Results) vs 'lived until 62' (Discussion): deceased age left null; (2) Family A has 'eight siblings' (Results) vs 'four siblings' (Abstract, referring to mutation carriers); (3) Family C 'consists of three generations' (Results) vs 'Two generation family' (Figure 1 legend); (4) Schwankhaus is spelled 'Schwankaus' in two places. No tables in the paper; no supplementary material.
